title: Early Detection of Battery Thermal Runaway Using Impedance and Gas Sensing
problem: Thermal runaway in lithium-ion packs is usually detected only after cell temperature has risen sharply, which leaves too little time to isolate the pack.
solution: A battery management unit measures cell impedance at several frequencies and reads a gas sensor that detects electrolyte vapour inside the pack housing. A classifier combines impedance drift and gas concentration trends to raise an early warning minutes before temperature rises, and the unit opens a contactor and signals the vehicle controller.

elements.text: A battery management unit that measures electrochemical impedance of lithium-ion cells at a plurality of frequencies
A gas sensor inside the pack housing that detects electrolyte vapour
A classifier that combines impedance drift and gas concentration trend to compute a thermal runaway risk score
An early warning raised when the risk score exceeds a threshold before cell temperature rises above a limit
A contactor that is opened in response to the early warning to isolate the pack
A signal sent to a vehicle controller identifying the affected module

dependent_features: Impedance measurement is done during idle periods
The risk threshold adapts to cell age
